The denominator is $-5+4\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-5-4\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-5-4\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{9\text{i}}{-5+4\text{i}} & =\frac{9\text{i}}{-5+4\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-5-4\text{i}}{-5-4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-45\text{i}-36{\text{i}}^{2}}{{5}^{2}-{4}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-45\text{i}-36(-1)}{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{36-45\text{i}}{25+16} \\  & =\frac{36-45\text{i}}{41}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{36-45\text{i}}{41}=\frac{36}{41}-\frac{45}{41}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
